chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them:
About a house and a dwelling that the sun does not reach, and urine reaches them, and ghusl from janabah is performed in them: may one perform salat in them when they have dried? He said: "Yes."
He said: And I asked him about salat between the graves— is it valid? So he said: "There is no harm in it."

key_terms.الدَّارِ: a dwelling or residence considered as a place of prayer
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, mentioned regarding whether sunlight reaches the place
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, the impurity affecting the place
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: a house or interior place under discussion for prayer
key_terms.الْقُبُورِ: graves, referring to the area between them
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is unobjectionable
key_terms.يُصَلَّى: to perform salat in that place

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat in a place touched by urine after it dries, and between graves?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on praying in places affected by urine and used for ghusl from janabah, indicating that salat is permitted there once the place has dried. It also states that performing salat between graves is unobjectionable.
